title: Deprecation wave scheduler and weighted variant roulette for pinned models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When customers pin to a model version we must support safe deprecation and capacity-driven fallbacks without causing large-scale user-facing regressions or sudden traffic surges to alternative variants. Existing fallback factories are deterministic and cause cascading cutovers during regional incidents or version retirements.

Goal: Implement a policy-driven, observable deprecation-wave scheduler together with a weighted (probabilistic) variant routing layer (aka 'variant roulette') for pinned versions. This system should: (1) minimize abrupt performance regressions during deprecation or capacity events, (2) provide gradual migration waves with configurable weights and safety guardrails, (3) integrate deprecation notice automation in Console and API, and (4) publish per-version performance profiles that inform fallback scoring.

Scope: server-side routing + control-plane scheduler + console surface + observability/alerts. Not in scope: new model training adjusters, customer migration tooling beyond suggested replacements and sample prompts.
implementation_notes: Add new 'deprecation_wave' resource in control plane: start_time, phases (list of weight maps), grace_period, escalation_policy

Implement weighted routing plugin in routing-service that accepts per-request constraints (region, cost_budget, latency_slo) and a variant_weight_map and returns chosen variant deterministically via request-id hashed sampling

Fallback scoring: combine normalized signals (latency_pctile / target_latency, cost_delta, compatibility_score, regional_capacity_score, deprecation_urgency) into a single score then convert to weight distribution with softmax temperature configurable per project
Expose 'predictive-impact' simulation endpoint that runs traffic mix samples against a candidate weight map and returns expected P50/P95 latency delta and token-cost delta to be shown in Console
Publish model version performance profile JSON to model-catalog: fields include seq_length_percentiles, token_throughput_per_gpu, quantization_profile, memory_kv_per_layer, known_regional_variance
Control-plane API to create/update deprecation waves; Console UI to visualize waves and trigger immediate 'freeze' or 'abort' actions
Telemetry: new dashboards and alerts: wave_impact_regression (P95 > baseline + threshold), migration_abort_rate, variant_thundering_rate
Safety: if P95 degradation exceeds X% for >Y minutes, automatic rollback to prior safe weight map and page on-call; can be disabled per-customer by explicit 'force-deprecate' flag
Data retention: keep per-wave simulation artifacts for 90 days for audit and debugging
Docs: design doc (Confluence), API spec (OpenAPI), Console mockups (Figma), migration playbook for solutions

acceptance_criteria: 1) Control plane accepts deprecation_wave definitions and stores them; 2) routing-service respects variant weights and performs hashed sampling, observable in request traces; 3) Simulation endpoint returns expected latency/cost deltas matching live A/B within 10% on synthetic workload; 4) Console shows wave timeline and allows pause/abort/force-deprecate; 5) Automatic rollback triggers when P95 exceeds configured threshold; 6) Model catalog contains performance profile for every pinned version used in experiments; 7) Documentation and runbook published and reviewed by SRE and Security
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: probabilistic routing creates variance in tail latency for individual users — Mitigation: enforce strict SLO guards and allow deterministic canary mode for high-risk customers
Risk: misconfigured wave can push too much traffic to a low-quality variant — Mitigation: require 'preview simulation' signoff before wave activation and soft launch at <5% by default
Risk: increased complexity for debugging customer incidents — Mitigation: capture per-request chosen_variant and weight_map_id in traces and surface in the Console request inspector

Risk: customers with strict pin guarantees may object — Mitigation: provide explicit 'pin-immutable' flag that disables automated waves for that customer (will require enterprise opt-in and legal acknowledgement)

review_feedback: PM (Sofia Martinez): prioritize simulation accuracy and customer-visible preview; require 'expected impact' to be computed before any >10% weight change
Design (Lina Gomez): simplify wave editor to 3 phased presets (soft, medium, hard) with advanced mode for power users
SRE (Tom Nguyen): insist on automatic rollback and runbook before enabling auto-escalation; suggested default P95 threshold = 25% over baseline
Security (Priya Rao): flagged telemetry fields that may contain customer identifiers; request pseudonymization and opt-out for enterprise customers
